clinicalPearls: A multifocal lymphatic malformation affecting multiple tissues and organs, categorised among the complex lymphatic anomalies in the ISSVA framework
Common sites include bone, spleen, mediastinum, lungs and soft tissue, and disease is often diffuse rather than focal
Bony involvement typically produces well-defined lytic lesions that, unlike Gorham-Stout disease, tend not to show progressive cortical destruction
Thoracic disease may cause chylothorax, pericardial effusion and respiratory compromise
It generally lacks the aggressive consumptive coagulopathy and haemorrhagic pleural fluid that characterise kaposiform lymphangiomatosis
Diagnosis rests on imaging distribution, histology showing abnormal lymphatic channels, and correlation within a multidisciplinary vascular anomalies service
Somatic activating variants in the PIK3CA pathway are described in many complex lymphatic anomalies
Sirolimus is a mainstay of medical therapy for symptomatic or progressive disease, supported by supportive management of effusions
reference.pathophysiology: Generalised lymphatic anomaly is a diffuse malformation of the lymphatic system in which abnormal, dilated lymphatic channels proliferate through multiple organs and tissues, characteristically involving bone, spleen and the thorax. It is a slow-flow lymphatic malformation rather than a tumour, and somatic activating variants in the PIK3CA-AKT-mTOR signalling pathway are implicated in many cases. Involvement of the thoracic lymphatics can lead to chylous effusions, while widespread visceral and skeletal disease produces the multiorgan picture; the bony lesions are typically non-progressive in contrast to Gorham-Stout disease.
additionalDifferentials: Metastatic malignancy or histiocytosis with multifocal lytic bone lesions
additionalInvestigations: Whole-body or targeted MRI to map soft-tissue, splenic and thoracic involvement
Plain radiographs and CT to characterise lytic bone lesions
Chest imaging and analysis of pleural or pericardial fluid for chyle
Biopsy with lymphatic markers (e.g. D2-40/podoplanin) for histological confirmation
Coagulation profile to distinguish from kaposiform lymphangiomatosis
Genetic analysis of PIK3CA-pathway variants where available
redFlags: Respiratory distress from chylothorax or large pericardial effusion
Rapidly accumulating or recurrent chylous effusions
Pathological fracture from extensive bony disease
Features suggesting transformation to a more aggressive lymphatic anomaly
reference.prognosis: Prognosis varies with the extent and site of disease; limited disease may remain stable, but extensive thoracic or visceral involvement with recurrent chylous effusions carries greater morbidity. Response to sirolimus is often favourable, though the condition is generally chronic and requires long-term surveillance.
pitfalls: Confusing it with Gorham-Stout disease and misjudging the risk of progressive osteolysis
Failing to check coagulation and thereby overlooking a diagnosis of kaposiform lymphangiomatosis
Underestimating thoracic involvement and the risk of chylous effusions
Attempting extensive surgery of diffuse disease rather than medical control
references: Mulliken and Young's Vascular Anomalies: Haemangiomas and Malformations
management: Medical therapy with the mTOR inhibitor sirolimus, targeting the implicated PIK3CA-AKT-mTOR pathway, to reduce lesion burden and effusions
Management of chylous effusions with a low-fat, medium-chain-triglyceride diet, drainage and pleurodesis or thoracic duct intervention for persistent leaks
Interventional sclerotherapy or surgical debulking for symptomatic or compressive focal lesions
Bone-directed treatment including bisphosphonates for painful or structurally significant lytic skeletal lesions
Respiratory support for pericardial or pleural disease causing cardiorespiratory compromise, with a coagulation profile to distinguish it from kaposiform lymphangiomatosis
Long-term surveillance imaging given the chronic course, monitoring visceral, splenic and thoracic involvement
Manage within a specialist multidisciplinary vascular anomalies service, with molecular analysis of PIK3CA-pathway variants to guide targeted therapy
